item.title: China's progress hailed across globe
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
China's progress hailed across globe Celebratory events highlight desire to further enhance cooperation As the People's Republic of China marked the 77th anniversary of its founding on Oct 1, celebrations in many parts of the world have brought together government officials and business leaders, who lauded China's development and called for enhanced bilateral cooperation. At a reception at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Wednesday to celebrate the anniversary, President Xi Jinping called on the nation to forge ahead with firm confidence and take solid steps to achieve the great national rejuvenation. Xi said: "We are immensely proud of the remarkable achievements of New China and fully confident in the bright prospects for Chinese modernization." In recent days, Chinese embassies and consulates worldwide have hosted a series of events to celebrate the National Day. Attending officials from various countries highly praised China's development achievements and expressed a desire to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation. At the United Nations' headquarters in New York, leading officials emphasized China's important role in multilateral cooperation. Guy Ryder, UN under-secretary-general for policy, said China is "a very active defender of multilateralism". "It's difficult to imagine, impossible to imagine, the United Nations without the People's Republic of China," Ryder said. Movses Abelian, UN under-secretary-general for General Assembly and Conference Management, also extended his greetings, offering wishes "for prosperity, harmony, and the best to all people of China".

item.title: EU tightens migration chain as return rules approved
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
EU tightens migration chain as return rules approved BRUSSELS - The European Union (EU) member states on Thursday gave final approval to a new regulation to accelerate the return of people with no legal right to stay, adding an enforcement mechanism to migration and asylum rules that took effect in June. Under the new Return Regulation, EU countries will operate under common return procedures, including a new European Return Order, and gain the option of establishing so-called "return hubs" in non-EU countries. According to the EU figure, around two in three people ordered to leave the bloc currently do not actually depart. The regulation complements the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, which took effect on June 12. The pact sets common rules for screening, asylum procedures, responsibility among member states and solidarity mechanisms, while the new regulation focuses on returning people found to have no right to stay. The European Commission earlier described returns as the "missing piece" of the pact, while European Parliament rapporteur Malik Azmani called return the "final piece in Europe's migration system." PRESSURE FOR GREATER CONTROL The tougher return rules come after a turbulent summer that again pushed migration high up Europe's agenda. On July 30 and 31, tens of thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, prompting Madrid to deploy the military and triggering calls from several European governments for tighter border controls. The crisis came only weeks after the migration pact entered into application and added urgency to a broader push for tougher enforcement. Claire Kumar, head of policy and senior research fellow at ODI Europe, told Xinhua that public concern over irregular migration was strongly linked to a perceived "lack of control," with people expecting governments to demonstrate that borders and migration rules were effectively managed. That pressure has become politically significant as mainstream parties face sustained pressure from right-wing and far-right forces advocating stricter migration controls, she added. Pressure for further restrictions is also growing. Greece on Thursday proposed a mechanism that would allow EU countries to temporarily suspend asylum applications during large-scale arrivals deemed instrumentalized, with Germany, Austria, Denmark and Poland open to considering the idea. These discussions suggest that the adoption of the Return Regulation may not mark the end of the EU's tightening migration agenda. ENFORCEMENT MEETS REALITY Yet passing a common return law does not guarantee a sharp rise in actual returns. The German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP) said in a recent analysis that return hubs are likely to remain limited in scale and heavily dependent on cooperation with third countries. It said that persistent obstacles include establishing migrants' identities, obtaining travel documents, securing cooperation from countries of origin, and finding third countries willing to host return facilities. Such problems cannot simply be bypassed by moving parts of the return process outside Europe. At the same time, Europe's aging economies still need migrant workers, Kumar said. She said that beneath increasingly restrictive political rhetoric, labor demand remains a powerful driver of migration. If adequate legal pathways are unavailable, workers may still fill those jobs through irregular or informal channels, increasing risks of exploitation and labor-market informality. The next test is implementation: whether the EU can turn its new legal powers into more effective returns while its aging economies continue to need migrant labor.

item.title: Wujiang River Gallery scenic area, Chongqing
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
Winding through the dramatic gorges of southeastern Chongqing, the Wujiang River showcases its most spectacular section, known as the "river gallery" — a poetic name for its roughly 100-kilometer scenic stretch. Towering cliffs and rugged peaks rise along the river, while the water shifts from calm and crystal-clear to swift and surging as it passes through the gorges. Ancient towns, ferry crossings, historic riverside paths, and cliffside burial sites remain along the banks, where dramatic natural scenery meets the region's rich cultural heritage. Together, they form a distinctive scenic corridor along the water in southeastern Chongqing. www.chinabound.cn Travel with ease in China, and with meaning.

item.title: Country on track for holiday travel boom
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
Country on track for holiday travel boom China is set to experience an unprecedented surge in travel demand during the seven-day National Day holiday, from Oct 1 to 7, with an expected 2.13 billion cross-regional trips across the country — averaging more than 300 million trips per day, said the Ministry of Transport. The travel volume is expected to peak on Thursday, with about 340 million trips recorded on the first day of the holiday, nearly twice the normal daily level. China's railway network is handling the heaviest passenger flow in its history. About 284 million passenger trips are expected during the 16-day railway holiday travel period from Sept 23 to Oct 8, with an average of about 13,000 passenger trains planned per day, according to national railway operator China State Railway Group. On Oct 1 alone, the national railway system is expected to transport 24.8 million passengers, with 2,324 additional trains deployed, it said. To accommodate the surge, railway operators have added about 700 overnight high-speed rail services on trunk lines including the Beijing-Guangzhou, Beijing-Shanghai and Beijing-Harbin routes. Major hubs such as Wuhan in Hubei province and Nanchang in Jiangxi province have launched round-the-clock operations. Additionally, according to the Civil Aviation Administration of China, from Sept 25 to Oct 7, the country's civil aviation sector is expected to transport 31.19 million passengers, averaging 2.4 million per day, an increase of 3.6 percent. The single-day peak is expected to exceed 2.6 million passenger trips, surpassing the level recorded in the same period last year. In the domestic market, air passenger traffic in major cities remains high, while traffic to distinctive tourist cities is growing rapidly, the administration said. In the international market, holiday ticket bookings rose 22.5 percent year-on-year. Neighboring countries remain popular tourist destinations, with flight volumes to Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam and Laos increasing by 20 percent. Long-haul international routes to the United Kingdom, Germany and Spain also saw a 15 percent increase, it said. Road travel, especially self-driving, is expected to account for more than 90 percent of all trips during the holiday, said Li Yang, vice-minister of transport. Highway traffic on the first day of the holiday is expected to reach 71 million vehicle trips, nearly 1.9 times the daily average in August of about 37 million, said Li, adding that people's willingness to travel and tour during the holiday will be strong. To prevent long and large-scale congestion at popular scenic spots and key road sections, the ministry has taken a series of measures. It has developed an AI-powered road network assessment tool using historical and forecast data to identify sections of road nationwide that may see serious congestion, Li said. Li Zhe, a traveler from Beijing, is planning a five-day self-driving trip to the Greater Khingan Mountains from Oct 2 to 6 with three friends he found on a social media platform. The route will pass through provincial-level regions of Hebei, Inner Mongolia and Heilongjiang, covering some 3,000 kilometers. "We are looking forward to enjoying the open road and we are not afraid of the tight schedule," he said.

item.title: Djokovic wowed by China Open crowds
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
Djokovic wowed by China Open crowds Tennis fuels holiday spending surge as organizers bank on record numbers Having seen and done almost everything in the sport around the world, 24-time major champion Novak Djokovic still marveled at the enthusiasm of Chinese fans after playing his first match in 11 years at the China Open on Wednesday. The Serbian great returned to the premier men's and women's combined tennis event in the Chinese capital for the first time since his appearance in 2015, only to realize that the public interest in the sport in China has soared far beyond his expectations. "A very pleasant surprise to see the full stadium in the first round," Djokovic said after beating Portugal's Nuno Borges 6-3, 7-6 (2) to reach the second round at the ATP 500 event, amid rousing cheers from the sellout crowd at the central court on the eve of China's National Day holiday. "I remember from playing here 11 years ago that people would come in big numbers to watch tennis and their favorite players. "They have a great tennis passion and tradition in this city. They have proven it once more today. They definitely exceeded my expectations," he said. Underlined by the electrifying vibe on the first night, which saw a capacity crowd of over 13,000 spectators swarm into the arena for Djokovic's opener, organizers expect to build on last year's all-time record of 360,000 total attendance to further cement the tournament's status as a must-visit holiday destination in town, not only for tennis fans but also tourists from home and abroad. "I think this is only the beginning of what we hope will be another successful year in the tournament's history," Li Xuhua, general manager of China Open Promotion Ltd, told China Central Television. To better tap into the consumption potential the tournament generates, the China Open has teamed up with partner hotels, restaurants, shopping malls and sightseeing landmarks to offer ticket holders extra discounts at surrounding businesses as a boost for sports tourism during the holiday. As the nation pushes the sports sector as a new driver for growth in the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-30), the sports entertainment business has been hailed by industry observers as a new frontier for stimulating consumption. "I think we still have a lot more potential to tap into, studying the cases of more established events, such as the four Grand Slams; tournament organizers should work closely with business partners to offer more entertainment products and services," said Wang Xueli, director of Tsinghua University's center for development of the sports industry. Anchored by the prestigious China Open, which also features a top-flight WTA 1000 tournament, the international tennis season is ushering in the autumn "China Swing" with five more events on the men's and women's professional circuits scheduled across the country through the end of this month. Combined revenues of nine tournaments during the same stretch last year exceeded 1 billion yuan ($149 million), with total ticket revenue hitting a record 250 million yuan, according to the General Administration of Sport of China. A glittering cast of international stars — Djokovic, newly crowned US Open champion Alexander Zverev of Germany, reigning Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen and women's world No 1 Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan — are all competing in Beijing this week before moving on to their next tournaments in China. "You are on your way to becoming a strong tennis nation," tennis legend Billie Jean King of the United States said last month in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, before the Billie Jean King Cup Finals. "The number of tournaments you have on the Asian swing is huge, as well as the investment you made. And that's going to pay off on all fronts."

item.title: Nation's travel landscape enters new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Nation's travel landscape enters new era Relaxed entry policies, digital payments infrastructure prove a magnet for global tourists As a hand-rowing boat drifts across Hangzhou's famed West Lake, Austrian traveler Florian Eisinger finds himself surrounded by willow-lined shores, ancient temples and centuries of history, with the gleaming skyline of one of China's most dynamic cities rising in the distance. For the 23-year-old who was visiting China for the first time in May, the scene captured what surprised him most about the country. "It was probably one of the most mesmerizing countries I visited in my life," Eisinger said. "From the cities to the landscapes to the people, everything was beyond what I had imagined." Two places stood out. "West Lake is just incredible scenery and a lot of history packed into one 'district', all while you have the very modern city of Hangzhou in the background," he said. "I did a boat tour over parts of the lake, and it was jaw-droppingly beautiful." The other place is Shanghai. Some streets, while being nestled within the bustling heart of the metropolis, especially in the evening, are incredibly beautiful, and it is surreal to imagine this being in one of the largest cities in the world, he said.

item.title: Leaders pay homage to fallen heroes on Martyrs' Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Leaders pay homage to fallen heroes on Martyrs' Day President Xi Jinping and other Party and State leaders attended a ceremony on Wednesday at Tian'anmen Square in central Beijing to present flower baskets to honor fallen national heroes, marking China's 13th Martyrs' Day. Established in 2014 and observed annually on Sept 30, one day before National Day, the day honors those who gave their lives for the liberation of the Chinese people and the nation's development. Since the first observance of Martyrs' Day, Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, has maintained the tradition of paying homage to fallen heroes on this day. On Wednesday morning, Xi and other leaders — Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng — joined representatives from all walks of life for the solemn ceremony in front of the Monument to the People's Heroes. At 10 am, all attendees sang the national anthem, followed by a moment of silence in tribute to the fallen heroes. Nine large flower baskets were placed in front of the monument. Xi and other leaders walked up to the foot of the monument, where he straightened the ribbons on the baskets. Then, they walked around the monument to pay tribute. Among the attendees carrying flowers were veterans, relatives of martyrs, recipients of awards and honorary titles, members of ethnic minority groups, students and children. Liu Jia, an associate professor at Beihang University's School of Marxism, watched the live broadcast of the ceremony. He said that observing Martyrs' Day is not only a solemn tribute to fallen heroes, but also a reminder of the hardships and unwavering convictions forged during China's revolutionary struggles. Liu noted that the commemoration came at a key moment, citing that this year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the CPC, the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March — an epic military trek from 1934 to 1936 that helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution — and the launch of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) for economic and social development. He said that the strength we gain from the Party's glorious history and the Long March will help drive new sci-tech progress today and inspire the younger generation. jihaisheng@chinadaily.com.cn
